text:
anya: Heads-up — hit a nasty onboarding UX bug: rotating a project key doesn't update the CLI in the current shell, so local devs keep calling with the old org key and get permission errors.

carlos: do we have a repro?

anya: yep: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=org_abc; export REDWOOD_PROJECT=proj-42; create project token in Console; run `rw auth rotate`. Node sample picks new token immediately but `rw` still uses org_abc until new shell.

kevin: that's the env vs cli-config precedence mismatch. CLI persisted "last-used" and wins over env in-process — that was intended for UX but causes rotation surprises.

anya: users are confused because errors are vague (401/403). They rotate keys and still can't access project resources. Support tickets piling up.

carlos: quick fixes: 1) make `rw auth rotate` update in-memory env resolution for current process unless `--no-shell`? 2) add `REDWOOD_DEBUG_AUTH=1` to print the lookup order and masked key id when resolving.

kevin: agree on debug. Also we should align precedence across SDKs/CLI: env -> credentials file -> metadata. Keep `last-used` for interactive suggestions only, don't let it override env in-process.

anya: docs need a tiny section: "how scoping works" and a troubleshooting snippet showing `REDWOOD_DEBUG_AUTH=1` output. Sample app README should call out `REDWOOD_PROJECT` behavior.

carlos: I'll open a small PR to: change precedence in CLI to match SDK, clear `~/.redwood/last-used` on successful rotate, and add debug log gated by env.

kevin: add unit tests covering env+file+cli-config combos in CI containerized runner. Also file a backend issue to make auth error payloads include the attempted key-id and scope info (masked) — won't leak secrets but makes support much faster.

devex-bot: Reminder: any change to credential resolution should include a migration note and changelog entry.

anya: timeline: PR by EOD from carlos, tests and docs follow early next week. Thanks! :clap:
